summary.short: Bill that would amend the Penal Code and Electoral Code to criminalise producing, disseminating or sharing AI-manipulated images of nudity or sexual acts, including sexual content involving candidates, with prison terms of 2 to 6 and 2 to 8 years and aggravations for certain victims. Effective on publication.
summary.long: Bill (PL 3821/2024) that would amend two codes. New Penal Code Art. 216-C criminalises manipulating, producing or disseminating, by any means, false nudity or sexual-act content generated by artificial intelligence or other technological means, punishable by reclusão of 2 to 6 years and a fine, unless a more serious crime applies. The penalty rises by one third to one half where the victim is a woman, child, adolescent, elderly or disabled person, and by one third to double where the content is disseminated en masse through social networks or digital platforms. New Electoral Code Art. 326-C criminalises creating, disseminating or sharing images manipulated by artificial intelligence or similar technology with explicit or simulated sexual content involving candidates, punishable by reclusão of 2 to 8 years and a fine. The penalty rises by one third to one half where the victim is a woman, elderly or disabled person. If the conduct is committed by a candidate, cassation of the candidacy registration or diploma is also imposed. The law would enter into force on the date of its publication (Art. 4). The document is the bill text, and its status is pending.

notes: The document is the bill text as submitted to the Câmara, signed by its president; the date line reads 'de fevereiro de 2025' with the day and month missing, and the text contains no legislative history. Target laws are not in the registry, so target_instrument_id is empty. Internal points: the registry title refers to 'manipulação digital de imagens', while Art. 1 and the new articles cover sexual content generated or manipulated by AI; the victim aggravation in new art. 216-C §1 covers 'criança, adolescente' but the one in art. 326-C §1 covers only women and elderly or disabled persons; art. 216-C applies only 'se o fato não constituir crime mais grave'. Art. 4 sets entry into force on the date of publication.

entities.note: The text names no firms, facilities or public bodies with an addressee, designated or beneficiary role; the Congresso Nacional and the Câmara dos Deputados appear only as enacting and signing bodies.

thresholds.note: The bill contains no numeric cutoff that changes scope, eligibility or exemption. The only numbers are penalty ranges (2 to 6 years; 2 to 8 years) and aggravation fractions (1/3 to 1/2; up to double), which are penalty amounts and therefore enforcement, not thresholds. Victim categories (woman, child, adolescent, elderly or disabled person) are not numerically defined in this text.

obligations.note: The operative provisions are criminal offences: new art. 216-C of the Penal Code (Art. 2) and new art. 326-C of the Electoral Code (Art. 3), with their penalties and aggravations. Under the annotation rules these are lists of infringements and penalties, which are coded as enforcement, not obligations. Art. 1 states the scope and Art. 4 the entry into force on publication. No other operative provision places a duty on a named addressee.
